cls: CLASS A — entity-registry divergence (parallel per-mover registries: render gate isOnGUI, force-bar roster, tacmap blips, selection eligibility, commandability)
contract:
For every home-commander mover in SP, the five registries must agree as a pure function of mover state. States and required tuple (onGUI, rosterIcon, selectable, tacmapBlip, commandable):
- ALIVE (exists, !destroyed, !disabled): onGUI=1 ⇒ icon PRESENT **unless the force bar is full** (ForceGroupBar caps at MAX_ICONS=16, forcegroupbar.h:22; addMech drops overflow at forcegroupbar.cpp:483-486 — bar-full is reported as advisory I1b, not a violation), selectable YES, blip YES, commandable YES.
- LINKUP-PENDING (exists, onGUI=0 — only mission.cpp:1956 destroyed-home part-spawn path creates this): icon ABSENT, NOT selectable (objmgr.cpp:4406 gate), NO blip, NOT commandable **by the player** — concretely: !isOnGUI() ⇒ !getSelected() AND NOT (pilot->getCurTacOrder()->code!=TACTICAL_ORDER_NONE && curTacOrder.origin==ORDER_ORIGIN_PLAYER) AND no roster icon. Origin scoping (tacordr.h:130, origin member :228) is deliberate: auto-powerup (warrior.cpp:7955-7960 handlePlayerOrder) and brain orders are ORDER_ORIGIN_SELF/COMMANDER; a self/commander-origin order on an off-GUI mover is emitted as ADVISORY, a player-origin order is a VIOLATION. (The #50 signature — invisible mover drag-selected and player-ordered — violates this row; verified pre-fix #50 trips I5 then I2 at the first audit tick.)
- SHUTDOWN (status==OBJECT_STATUS_SHUTDOWN, onGUI=1): icon PRESENT (same bar-full carve-out), selectable YES, blip YES with ring=0 (gametacmap.cpp:432), commandable YES (auto-powerup warrior.cpp:7955-7960 is intentionally ungated — the upstream selection gate is the only defense; hence row 2's invariant).
- DISABLED-NOT-DESTROYED (salvageable, #42b-adjacent): while ObjectManager-registered and exists, getAppearance() != NULL (appearance teardown while salvageable would make hover/info/salvage unreachable even through the narrow missiongui.cpp:2116 guard); excluded from select-all (missiongui.cpp:4668) is CORRECT and asserted. NOTE (corrected claim): the HISTORICAL #42b bug — guard widened to bare isDisabled(), nulling targets that HAD valid appearances — is invisible to this runtime row and is caught ONLY by static rule S4 pinning the guard shape.
- TRADED-TO-HOME / CAPTURED (mission.cpp:2336 tradeMover with newCommanderID==home): falls under ALIVE/SHUTDOWN rows after the mission.cpp:2362 re-add. tradeMover never touches setOnGUI; this is sound today because every non-home part spawns onGUI=1 (mission.cpp:1965/1970) — asserted as I1 coverage, exercised by the MC2_SOAK_SALVAGE_TRADEMOVER fixture.
- REMOVED/DEAD: every ForceGroupIcon::unit (Mover* at code/mechicon.h:129) must round-trip through ObjectManager registration (getByWatchID pattern, missiongui.cpp:2092). Destroyed-but-registered movers legitimately KEEP their icon through the death animation (icon deleted only via removeMover, forcegroupbar.cpp:514, called from mission.cpp:2326/2339 before freeMover :2331) — the check is registration, never !destroyed.
- SAVE/LOAD: isOnGui is restored raw from save data (code/mover.cpp:7650) while the interface roster is rebuilt separately (ControlGui::initMechs, controlgui.cpp:2283) — coherence must re-hold by the first audit tick after load; the runtime audit is the detector for drift on this path.
Write path contract: isOnGui may only change at the allowlisted sites — setOnGUI callers {mission.cpp:1956/1965/1970/2218; mech.cpp:6009} plus direct member writes {mover.cpp:2382 (Mover::init default), mover.cpp:7650 (load restore)}; roster membership only at {mission.cpp:2193/2362, mech.cpp:6006 (add); mission.cpp:2326/2339 (remove)}. All eight verified as the exhaustive current set.
mechanism:
THREE layers, static-first per house rules. All anchors below re-verified against A:/Games/mc2-issue-fixes on 2026-07-16.
[1] STATIC CHECKER scripts/check-mover-registry-coherence.sh (new, joins the run_check rows in scripts/check-contracts.sh:91+). Rules, any hard hit = exit 1:
  S1 setOnGUI + direct-write chokepoint allowlist — `setOnGUI(` call sites outside the three definitions (code/mover.h:1783, code/gameobj.h:1191, code/gvehicl.h:538) must be exactly {code/mission.cpp:1956,1965,1970,2218; code/mech.cpp:6009} (verified exhaustive). CORRECTED from prior draft: direct `isOnGui =` member writes DO exist outside the headers — code/mover.cpp:2382 (init) and code/mover.cpp:7650 (load restore) — so the write scan uses member-write pattern `(^|[^.>[:alnum:]_])isOnGui[[:space:]]*=[^=]` (which also excludes the serializer LHS `data->isOnGui = ...` at mover.cpp:7490) with allowlist {mover.cpp:2382, mover.cpp:7650, gvehicl.h:540, mover.h:1785}. A new write site turns the repo red until consciously allowlisted with a pairing review.
  S2 write-pairing windows — mech.cpp setOnGUI(true) must have `mission->missionInterface->addMover(this)` within 10 lines above (verified: mech.cpp:6006→6009); mission.cpp:2218 setOnGUI(true) must have `missionInterface->addMover(mover)` earlier in the same function (verified :2193); `missionInterface->removeMover` sites must be exactly {mission.cpp:2326, 2339} and `missionInterface->addMover` sites exactly {mission.cpp:2193, 2362; mech.cpp:6006} (both verified exhaustive); ObjectManager->freeMover's sole game-side caller (mission.cpp:2331) must be preceded by removeMover in-function (verified: :2326).
  S3 read-gate pinning, TRIMMED (adversarial finding: 11 hard pins doubled refactor false-positive surface with no added detection) — HARD pins only the three read gates with distinct symptom classes: GameObjectManager::moverInRect body contains `isOnGUI()` (the #50 fix, objmgr.cpp:4406 — selection class), tacmap home-commander branch keeps it (gametacmap.cpp:429 — blip class), ControlGui::initMechs keeps it (controlgui.cpp:2283 — roster-rebuild/load-reconciliation class). The four pick paths (objmgr.cpp:3984/4054/4094/4319) and select-all trio (missiongui.cpp:4657/4668/4678) are ADVISORY (grep emits WARN, exit stays 0): their drift is runtime-caught by I2/I5 in every tier1 run.
  S4 #42b guard shape — hover guard must remain the narrow form `target->isDisabled() && !target->getAppearance()` (verified at code/missiongui.cpp:2116); bare `target->isDisabled())` in that window is forbidden. THIS RULE IS THE SOLE DEFENSE against historical #42b (runtime I3 cannot see it) — never demote.
  S5 link-up gate shape — BattleMech::update link-up branch keys on `!isOnGUI()` alone (verified `if (!isOnGUI())` at code/mech.cpp:5977), forbidden pattern `status == OBJECT_STATUS_SHUTDOWN &&` in that window — reverting the #50 latch fix goes red.
  Precedent for anchor-pinned caller checks: scripts/check-asset-scale-callers.sh (exists, verified).
[2] RUNTIME AUDIT — MC2_MOVER_COHERENCE_AUDIT, default OFF, static-getenv latch, mirrors bridgeEmitMoverState (namespace mission.cpp:512-520, function :554, called at :1084-1085), new static auditMoverCoherence(scenarioTime) beside it, ~1 Hz. Per home-commander SP mover:
  I1 onGUI && exists && !destroyed ⇒ roster icon present OR iconCount==MAX_ICONS (bar-full emits ADVISORY I1b instead — forcegroupbar.cpp:483-486 silently drops the 17th mover in release; without this carve-out I1 false-positives on salvage-heavy missions).
  I2 !onGUI ⇒ no icon && !getSelected() && no PLAYER-origin tac order (origin==ORDER_ORIGIN_PLAYER, tacordr.h:130/:228; self/commander-origin logged as advisory — avoids false positives from ORDER_ORIGIN_SELF auto-powerup, warrior.cpp:7955-7960, and brain orders). Catches invisible-but-commandable (#50 signature).
  I3 isDisabled && !isDestroyed && exists ⇒ getAppearance()!=NULL. CORRECTED SCOPE: catches appearance-teardown-while-salvageable (#42b-ADJACENT class); does NOT and cannot catch historical #42b (that was a guard-shape bug with valid appearances — S4's job).
  I4 every ForceGroupIcon::unit (Mover* at code/mechicon.h:129; ForceGroupBar is a friend) round-trips through ObjectManager registration (getByWatchID pattern, missiongui.cpp:2092). Registration only — destroyed movers legitimately keep icons through death animation.
  I5 getSelected() ⇒ onGUI (selection-gate drift caught between the trimmed S3 anchors — this is what lets S3 shrink).
  Roster query accessor: `bool ForceGroupBar::hasMover(const Mover*) const` walking icons[0..iconCount) (private members at forcegroupbar.h:83-84, public getter beside getIconCount at :63), surfaced as ControlGui::rosterHasMover (beside addMover decl, controlgui.h:142) and MissionInterfaceManager passthrough (beside addMover/removeMover inlines, missiongui.h:226-227; controlGui member :145). All header anchors verified.
  Violations emit BOTH mc2_diag::writeEvent("MOVER_COHERENCE", ...) and one stdout line `[MOVER_COHERENCE] VIOLATION rule=I2 part=...` (advisories print `ADVISORY` not `VIOLATION`), deduped per (mover,rule) per mission; mission-end summary event {checked,violations,advisories}.
  Registration: kAuxEnvVars entry (table at RenderCore/RendererFeatureRegistry.h:599; precedent MC2_LINKUP_TRACE entry at ~:1813-1822, EnvVarKind::Trace default false); docs/tier1_env_vars.md row; run_smoke.py Popen env allowlist (the allowlist actually spans ~:1170-1410 — add the var there or Popen drops it); `sh scripts/check-env-registry.sh` (exists, verified) must stay PASS.
[3] CHOKEPOINT (optional slice 2): fold I1-I5 into debug asserts at the two pairing chokepoints (mission.cpp:2218 addMover tail, mech.cpp:6009 link-up). Adversarial note: a SINGLE chokepoint assert inside Mover::setOnGUI (mover.h:1783) was evaluated and REJECTED — setOnGUI runs at part-spawn before the interface roster exists, and #50 was a READ-path bug (drag-select of a never-transitioned mover) that no write-time assert can see; the layered static+sampled design is the minimal shape that covers both write and read drift.
smoke_integration: run_smoke.py force-sets MC2_MOVER_COHERENCE_AUDIT=1 in the child env for --tier runs (read-only audit; shipping default stays OFF — same spirit as MC2_DEBUG_STATE_DUMP in the canonical command), and the var is added to the Popen passthrough allowlist (run_smoke.py ~:1170-1410) so it survives into the child. Detection via the STDOUT marker, independent of the operator's MC2_DIAG_TAGS: post-run, scan each mission log for `[MOVER_COHERENCE] VIOLATION` exactly like the VEG-SMOKE-FLOOR scanner (verified scripts/run_smoke.py:104-123) and hard-fail on any hit (verified precedents: VEG hard fail :2135-2141, fingerprint hard fail :2144-2150). `ADVISORY` lines are surfaced in the report but never fail the run (this is what makes the I1b bar-full and I2 self-origin carve-outs safe). The diag-state section (verified :2287+) gains an advisory liveness scan for the MOVER_COHERENCE summary event (WARN if the audit never ran). Cost: ~1 Hz walk over ~24-60 movers with an O(iconCount<=16) membership probe — immaterial for tier1; gate-off path is one static bool. mc2_08 (the #50 link-up mission) is the nightly add-on since tier1's five missions may not exercise LINKUP-PENDING; tier1 still exercises ALIVE/SHUTDOWN/DISABLED rows plus all static rules every run, and check-mover-registry-coherence.sh runs in every check-contracts.sh invocation with zero runtime dependency.
residual_risk: (1) HISTORICAL #42b HAS NO RUNTIME DETECTION — the adversarial review confirmed I3 would have passed throughout the original bug (targets had valid appearances; the guard shape was the defect). Static S4 plus interactive hover testing are the only defenses; a semantically equivalent guard rewrite that S4's pattern doesn't match could slip through. (2) 1 Hz sampling misses divergences that self-heal within a second — layer-3 write-time asserts close this. (3) SP home-commander only: MPlayer parallel rosters (mission.cpp:1936-1940 spawn-side, tradeMover MP branches :2341-2356) unaudited; MP drift invisible to tier1. (4) I2's origin scoping means an invisible-mech bug that manifests ONLY through ORDER_ORIGIN_SELF/COMMANDER orders (e.g., a brain scripting an off-GUI home mover) downgrades to an advisory — visible in the report but not red. Accepted to kill the auto-powerup/brain false-positive class; revisit if an advisory ever correlates with a field report. (5) Save/load restores isOnGui raw (mover.cpp:7650); reconciliation depends on the load path re-running ControlGui::initMechs — the only initMechs caller found is logistics.cpp:873 (mission-start path), and I could NOT verify that in-mission quicksave/load re-invokes it; tier1 never loads saves, so this row gets runtime coverage only if a load-fixture mission is added. The audit WILL catch post-load drift when it runs, but nothing in tier1 exercises it. (6) Anchor-pinned greps still go red on legitimate refactors (loud false positive, never silent pass) — surface halved by trimming S3 to three hard pins, accepted per the can't-regress-silently preference. (7) Registry-state coherence only, not pixel truth (alpha/icon-art wrongness invisible to I1-I5). (8) tier1 may never instantiate LINKUP-PENDING or mid-mission trade — mc2_08 / MC2_SOAK_SALVAGE_TRADEMOVER cover rows 2/6 nightly; S1-S5 guard those paths on every commit. (9) ABL-spawned movers (verified ablmc2.cpp:3155 routes through Mission::addMover, so the :2193/:2218 pairing covers them at write time) are audit-covered only from the next tick after spawn. (10) Unverified minutiae: exact line of the MC2_LINKUP_TRACE registry entry (region ~1813-1822 confirmed, cited 1818-1823 is a few lines off) and check-contracts.sh run_check rows extending past :124 — neither affects enforceability.

cls: CLASS B — silent asset-load failure (appearance-shape loads or icon-atlas index resolutions fail; engine renders nothing/garbage and keeps going). PROVENANCE CORRECTED BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: the two cited historical bugs do NOT belong to this class and the original design would not have caught either. #50 (invisible reinforcement Atlas, mc2_08) was a gameplay link-up latch — assets verified intact, appearance loaded fine, mech hidden by selection/power-up logic (fixed f659d48f; .claude/ISSUE-FIXES-STATUS.md row 2 + .claude/issue-reply-drafts.md:35-58) — the mission_ready appearance audit would have PASSED on it. #43 (gray-block AAR icons) was IN-BOUNDS atlas mis-scaling on column-extended atlases, fixed by AssetScale::blitFactorFor and already recurrence-locked by the shipped [ASSET_SCALE v1] selftest + oob_blit red bucket (row 3, commit 16b8011d) — an index-OOB guard would not have fired. The class instead stands on direct code evidence: mclib/msl.cpp's deliberate fail-soft -1 returns ('leave the mech without an appearance rather than crashing', msl.cpp:260-270) with ~33 return-ignoring load call sites (grep-verified complete list below), plus the residual icon index-OOB wrap/blank class left open by CRASH-HARDEN-OBJECTIVE-ICON-1. Secondary value, honestly stated: the always-on [ASSET_LOAD] lines and the audit would have DISAMBIGUATED #50 in minutes (the actual fix required manually verifying atlas.ini/atlas.tgl/object2.pak intact — work the audit automates), which is diagnostic value, not prevention.
contract: Every appearance-shape load either succeeds, or is classified and logged: a file-present-but-unparseable failure (parse_fail) and a missing REQUIRED base shape (required_missing) each emit exactly one rate-limited machine-parseable "[ASSET_LOAD v1] event=..." line with asset path/context and — for required slots, under default-ON killswitch — populate a VISIBLE magenta placeholder that is guaranteed renderable on BOTH legacy and GPU-batcher paths; a missing OPTIONAL file (arms, shadows, damage shapes, anims — normal stock degradation) logs only under a trace gate and keeps existing delete/NULL behavior byte-identical. Every icon-atlas index resolution that lands out of the atlas's real row/column range emits one "[ASSET_LOAD v1] event=icon_oob" line (always) while returning the legacy-computed cell unchanged (placeholder tile substitution only under opt-in gate — legacy wrap is load-bearing for MC2X content per mechicon.cpp:365-367). Additionally (default-OFF gate, armed in tier1 only after a 24-map failed=0 baseline): at mission_ready every spawned renderable object has a non-NULL appearance whose base shape actually loaded. No new shape-load call site may bypass the checked helper or the loader-side logging (statically enforced).
mechanism:
FIVE PARTS; the big structural revision vs. the reviewed draft is PART 0 — logging moves INSIDE the loader (one chokepoint covers all 33 current callers and every future one), and call-site edits shrink to the ~17 Required base-slot sites only.

PART 0 — loader-internal logging chokepoint (mclib/msl.cpp, all anchors verified): instrument the fail-soft returns themselves — LoadTGMultiShapeFromASE missing-file (msl.cpp:~673), bad ASE header (:~700), missing material block (:~713); LoadBinaryCopy open-fail (:204-205) and unknown-nodeType abort (:267-269, which already printfs); LoadFromFile via assimp (contract at mclib/assimp_importer.h:20-28). Classify: event=parse_fail (file existed, content bad) logged ALWAYS, rate-limited per unique path + process cap 32; event=file_missing logged only under MC2_ASSET_TRACE — because missing optional files are NORMAL stock degradation (arms mech3d.cpp:505/:515 already delete-on-fail; shadow :485; fall-damage :539/:554 GetNumShapes-checked; anims :601 'not a problem!' by design; bdactor.cpp:1022/:5531; gvactor.cpp:269/:284; genactor.cpp:148 — all verified) and an always-on file_missing line would red-bucket healthy tier1 runs (the reviewed draft's biggest false-positive). Grep-verified there are NO other callers of the three load entry points anywhere in code/ mclib/ editor/ GameAdapters/ GameOS/ Viewer/ EditorBridge/, so this chokepoint is complete and also closes the reviewed draft's residual-risk #4 for logging.

PART 1 — checked helper for REQUIRED base slots only (new mclib/tgl_load_guard.h/.cpp): tglLoadShapeChecked wrapping the stock ASE call, plus tglVerifyShapeLoaded(shape, rc, ctx, failFlag) post-check form for the opt-in import branches. Failure = (rc != NO_ERR || GetNumShapes()==0), the pattern already used at mech3d.cpp:541/:556, bdactor.cpp:1024, genactor.cpp:150 (verified). On failure: (1) "[ASSET_LOAD v1] event=required_missing" always; (2) MC2_VERIFY fire (macro at GameOS/include/mc2_verify.h:~53; kLogLineCap=64 at GameOS/gameos/mc2_verify.cpp:30 — verified); (3) under MC2_ASSET_FAILLOUD (default-ON killswitch, MC2_TERRAIN_TESS precedent) populate a magenta placeholder box — REVISED: the placeholder MUST register a real 4x4 magenta texture through mcTextureManager and set valid handles, NOT numTextures=0, because the GPU static-prop/mech batchers cull packets with layerForPacket=-1 (documented at bdactor.cpp:1031-1043, verified) — a textureless placeholder would itself be invisible on the modern path, defeating the contract; (4) set AppearanceType::baseShapeLoadFailed (mclib/apprtype.h:~40, verified). Stock byte-identical: no stock base shape fails, so the branch is cold. REQUIRED sites (grep-verified complete, fixing 5 omissions in the reviewed draft): mech3d.cpp:439/:462 ASE + :434/:457 LoadFromFile import branches; :755/:766/:777 sensor statics; bdactor.cpp:868/:892 + import branch via loadBuildingImportSourceWithSidecarAxis (bdactor.cpp:336 — MISSED by the draft's enumeration though its own checker would flag it); tree :5353/:5382 + :5349/:5378 import; gvactor.cpp:233/:254 + :229/:250 import, :436/:447 sensors; genactor.cpp:121/:125. Optional sites get NO code change (Part 0 covers them) — only a checker exemption tag.

PART 2 — chokepoint backstop: AppearanceTypeList::getAppearance (verified sole factory at mclib/apprtype.cpp:250, init calls ~:314/:341/:368/:395): after init, baseShapeLoadFailed → one "[ASSET_LOAD v1] event=appr_type_fail name=<appearFile>" (inherently once-per-type via the cache); catches future subclasses/loaders that bypass everything. Existing [LOADRACE] NULL logging at apprtype.cpp:264-286 (verified) already covers NULL-return paths.

PART 3 — icon-index chokepoints, REVISED to zero-behavior-change by default: (a) UV path: code/icon_atlas_cell.h (verified: header-only extraction, cellForIndex currently takes atlas WIDTH only) gains cellForIndexChecked adding an atlasH parameter for the row bound; on OOB it returns the LEGACY-COMPUTED cell unchanged + *oob=true (the draft's return-cell-0 would swap legit high-index mod icons for icon 0 on any false positive) and callers (code/logisticsmechicon.cpp:~153, code/mechlistbox.cpp — both verified using the shared header) emit event=icon_oob. CAUTION baked into tests: cellW/cellH come from widget size, so the row bound must be validated in tools/icon_atlas_harness/ against retail 256x256, MC2X 512, and MCO 1024/40 dims before the smoke bucket counts icon_oob red. (b) CPU blit path: shared entry guard iconTileChecked at the three mechicon.cpp blits (:352-372, :571-593, :1290-1304 — verified, already bounds-guarded-to-blank) keyed on AssetScale keys (:483/:~1239/:~1678 verified); log always, magenta tile only under MC2_ICON_FAILLOUD=1 default-OFF (wrap semantics load-bearing per mechicon.cpp:365-367, verified).

PART 4 — post-mission-load audit: MC2_APPEAR_AUDIT (default OFF, kAuxEnvVars at RenderCore/RendererFeatureRegistry.h:~599, verified) hooked beside mission_phase_mark("mission_ready") at code/mission.cpp:~4811 (verified); O(N) pass via ObjectManager getNumObjects/get (code/objmgr.h:327/:504, verified); emits [APPEAR_AUDIT v1] missing/summary lines. REVISED arming discipline: whether any object class legitimately has NULL appearance at mission_ready is UNVERIFIED, so the gate ships observational and is added to the tier1 allowlist only after a 24-map baseline run shows failed=0.

PART 5 — static checker: scripts/check-tgl-load-callers.sh wired into the run_check list (scripts/check-contracts.sh:91+, verified), modeled on scripts/check-asset-scale-callers.sh:15-35 (verified — NOTE: that script uses grep -v path/name exclusions, not comment tags; the `// TGL-LOAD-EXEMPT(<reason>)` / `// TGL-LOAD-VERIFIED` tag convention here is new but trivial). P1: raw ->LoadTGMultiShapeFromASE( / ->LoadFromFile( / ->LoadBinaryCopy( outside msl.cpp+guard and untagged = FAIL. Optional sites get one-line exempt tags citing loader-side logging. P2 presence asserts as drafted (cellForIndexChecked, iconTileChecked x3, appr_type_fail marker, audit hook marker). THREE new env vars (the draft said two): MC2_ASSET_FAILLOUD, MC2_ICON_FAILLOUD, MC2_APPEAR_AUDIT (+optional MC2_ASSET_TRACE) — all covered by existing scripts/check-env-registry.sh per the discipline at .claude/ISSUE-FIXES-STATUS.md:29-33 (verified). Helper in mclib so mc2/EditRel/mc2_launcher all link.
smoke_integration: Pattern verified end-to-end in the repo: "[ASSET_SCALE v1] event=oob_blit" counted at scripts/smoke_lib/logparse.py:140 (draft said :141 — off by one), red `asset_oob` bucket at scripts/smoke_lib/gates.py:67-68, per-mission `allow_asset_oob` override at smoke_lib/manifest.py:33 + parse at :81-84 (all verified). Add the same way: (1) `asset_load_fail` bucket counting event=parse_fail + event=required_missing + event=appr_type_fail ONLY — deliberately NOT bare event=file_missing, so normal optional-slot degradation (missing arms/shadows/anims on stock units, prevalence unverified) cannot red-flag healthy runs; these lines are always-on and load-time-only, so every existing tier1 run goes red the moment a stock base shape stops loading, at zero steady-state cost inside the 30 s play window; manifest override `allow_asset_load_fail` for deliberately-broken mod lanes. (2) `icon_oob` bucket armed only after the harness OOB cases validate the row bound against all three shipped atlas geometries (false-OOB risk from widget-size-as-cell-size). (3) `appear_audit` bucket matching "[APPEAR_AUDIT v1] event=missing", armed by adding MC2_APPEAR_AUDIT=1 to the tier1 passthrough allowlist ONLY after a 24-map failed=0 baseline (registration+allowlist+docs discipline per .claude/ISSUE-FIXES-STATUS.md:29-33, verified). Hook cost: one object-list scan at mission_ready (code/mission.cpp:~4811, verified) — immaterial. Nightly visual-capture sets make the magenta placeholder human-visible — now actually true on the GPU path because the placeholder carries a real registered texture (layerForPacket=-1 cull, bdactor.cpp:1031-1043). The static checker fails scripts/check-contracts.sh at commit time, so a new unchecked load site never reaches smoke.
residual_risk: REFUTATIONS INCORPORATED (what the draft claimed but could not deliver): (a) does NOT prevent #50-class bugs — that was a gameplay visibility latch with assets intact; this design only disambiguates such reports faster; (b) does NOT prevent #43-class in-bounds mis-scaling — that guard is the already-shipped ASSET_SCALE selftest/oob_blit machinery; this design covers the adjacent index-OOB and load-failure classes. SURVIVING RESIDUALS: (1) load-time only — per-instance runtime texture resolution (bdactor.cpp:1031-1043 class), eviction, and corrupt-after-fileExists anim content still degrade silently to frozen poses/wrong textures; (2) wrong-but-loaded geometry (tipped-Flea class, mech3d.cpp:375-390 comment verified) passes every check — only visual capture catches it; (3) the audit and icon-tile substitution are gated; if never armed in tier1, only the always-on parse_fail/required_missing/icon_oob lines are self-enforcing; (4) a future loader entry point with a new method name evades both the msl.cpp chokepoint and the grep until added — mitigated by the getAppearance backstop, which catches any empty base shape regardless of loader; (5) whole-TGA UI art with no index math remains out of scope (mechicon.cpp:485-489 Assert path, verified). COULD NOT VERIFY: which stock units actually lack optional arm/shadow/damage/anim files (the missing-vs-parse split is designed to be safe under either answer, but the file_missing trace gate's usefulness depends on it); whether any object class legitimately reports NULL appearance at mission_ready (hence the audit baseline requirement); that the magenta placeholder actually renders through GpuMechBatcher/StaticPropBatcher end-to-end (design mandates a real texture per the layerForPacket evidence, but only a runtime probe proves it); and the exact identity of the historical incident behind msl.cpp's 'leave the mech without an appearance' fail-soft comment — the class's true origin bug is undocumented in the issue ledger.

cls: C — split rendering paths silently diverging (tess/non-tess terrain, textured/untextured gos quad shaders, GL/VK islands, legacy/ImGui panels)
contract: Every known path-pair must share its contract at a single chokepoint or carry machine-checkable markers proving agreement. (1) COLOR (issue #24 class): the repo has three legitimate swizzle conventions, so the invariant is per-PROGRAM, not per-file — the Color chain from packed-BGRA attribute to FragColor applies an ODD number of .bgra swizzles (exactly one, in VS or FS), and any VS write of Color from RGBA-space computed data is pre-swizzled so the paired FS's read convention still nets identity; enforced as (a) every ACTIVE FS read of varying Color applies exactly one .bgra per read UNLESS the program's row in the in-checker convention table declares VS-side swizzle, and (b) enumerated sibling FAMILIES (textured/untextured/lighted gos quad FS set; water fast/fast-MDI VS pair) must have IDENTICAL declared conventions — one member drifting (the exact #24 failure: one FS of the pair losing .bgra) is a red check. (2) DEPTH (post-divide-fudge class, the deleted water-recession/z-fight root mechanism documented at gos_terrain_surface.vert:24-41 — NOT issue #34, which was near-plane clipping): all GLSL depth-fudge/bias constants are single-sourced in shaders/include/terrain_depth_bias.hglsl, lockstep with mclib/terrain_depth_bias.h on the shared-name intersection (C++-only back-compat alias WATER_DEPTH_FUDGE at terrain_depth_bias.h:80 allowlisted); every GLSL application site uses the pre-divide form `clip.z += K * clip.w`; the banned post-divide form (`screen.z = clip.z*rhw + K`) never reappears IN SHADERS (the CPU raster path legitimately biases post-divide per terrain_depth_bias.h:9-10 and is out of scope); local constant mirrors are allowed only with a LOCKSTEP-MIRROR marker whose value the checker verifies equals the header; tess and non-tess terrain emitters carry the identical normalized bias-application line so a future non-zero fudge moves both paths together. (3) PREDICATE (issue #34 class): the raw feature tokens RendererFeature::TerrainTessellation / MC2_TERRAIN_TESS appear ONLY in the allowlist {RenderCore/RendererFeatureRegistry.h, GameOS/gameos/gameos_graphics.cpp, GameOS/include/gameos.hpp, GameOS/gameos/gos_mech_killswitch.h (comments), tests/unit/test_rendercore.cpp}; all other code reaches tess-coupled behavior only through the two named predicates — gos_IsModernShadowPathActive() for shadow/near-plane behavior (the #34 fix) and gos_IsTerrainTessellationActive() for genuinely-tess-dependent work (GPU-mech leaf-skip) — freezing the chokepoint that #34's 8 divergent sites were converted to. (4) PAIRS: every enumerated path-pair has a manifest entry with content-hash stamps; every file under shaders/vulkan/ must appear either as a pair member or as an explicit island-only entry with a stated reason (fullscreen.vert/.frag and the VK-only .vert files have no GL siblings); editing either side of a pair without re-stamping fails CI.
